title: Directional KL Divergences between Counterfactual Outcome Laws near a Sparse Support Boundary
banked_reason: Sound matching forward n^-2/5 and reverse n^-1/2 risk and honest-interval-length orders on the declared class; below fixed field novelty floor, projected paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4 and not salvageable in scope.
gap_reasons: Significance is limited by the known one-dimensional covariate law, fixed endpoint, known quadratic exponent, and prescribed Lipschitz envelopes; these results do not establish adaptation or a general support-sensitive inference framework.

The forward certificate's 3000 n^{-2/5} term alone forces the reported intervals to equal [0,5] through approximately 2.8 billion observations, and the delivered package contains no reproducible performance study demonstrating useful alternative calibration.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matching n^-2/5 forward and n^-1/2 reverse absolute-risk and honest-interval-length orders with unknown propensity, original-record upper certificates and same-class lower comparisons. The mathematical review passed after primary-source attestation, but the novelty review found subfield tier, projected score 6.8 below 7.4, and no bounded repair within scope; an independent terminal-validity consult concurred. Banking stopped before F1; no Lean formalization or kernel proof was produced. The reviewed derivation remains reusable for an explicitly broader future research program.
tldr: Treatment can change an outcome distribution near a sparse support boundary even when treatment probabilities are uniformly positive. The project determines the sharp absolute-risk and honest connected-interval-length orders for both directional KL summaries on one normalized quadratic-boundary causal model. Attainment must come from the original observational records, retain the unknown propensity and continuous outcome confounding, and match legal observed-likelihood converses. The rates and their comparison are derived outputs. The formal score contrast motivates boundary regularization but does not replace its proof.
gap: The causal density-effect framework gives a regular one-step starting point, while inspected continuous KL and density-ratio results exclude the forward boundary witness through ratio or tail control. No inspected theorem supplies the declared original-record two-direction risk and finite-sample honest-length result.
fill: A boundary-weighted observable correction and exact count conditioning must deliver a uniform public certificate. Legal normalized likelihood comparisons then decide the attainable estimation and honest-length orders without adding oracle or nuisance-negligibility premises.
